title: Go: HTML Templates
description: Master Go's html/template package with template parsing, data rendering, nested templates, and custom functions.

steps.title: Parse and execute a template
steps.description: Create a template string `Hello {{.Name}}!` and parse it with `template.New("hello").Parse(tmplStr)`. Execute with `tmpl.Execute(os.Stdout, data)` where data is a struct with a `Name` field. Print the parsed template name using `fmt.Println`.
hints: template.New creates a new template with a name
Parse can fail with invalid syntax
Execute writes output to the writer (use os.Stdout)

steps.title: Template data with structs and maps
steps.description: Create a template that renders a struct with `Name`, `Age`, and `Items []string`. Use `{{range .Items}} {{.}} {{end}}` to iterate. Print the rendered output using `fmt.Printf("Rendered: %s\n", buf.String())` after writing to `bytes.Buffer`.
hints: {{range}} iterates over slices; {{.}} is the loop variable
Struct fields must be exported to be accessible

steps.title: Conditional rendering
steps.description: Add `{{if .IsAdmin}}` and `{{else}}` blocks to a template. Also use `{{with .Profile}}` to scope the context. Print both branches using `fmt.Printf("Admin: %t\n", ...)` to verify conditional logic works.
hints: {{if}} evaluates truthiness (nil, 0, false, empty are false)
{{with}} sets dot to the value and executes block if non-empty

verification.failureMessage: Print the admin status and profile information.

steps.title: Nested templates
steps.description: Use `{{define "name"}}` and `{{template "name" .}}` to create a base layout with a content block. Parse multiple templates with `template.ParseFiles` or template strings. Print the combined rendered output using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Define templates inside the same Parse call
{{template "name" pipeline}} executes a named template with pipeline

verification.failureMessage: Print the rendered layout with embedded content.

steps.title: Template functions with FuncMap
steps.description: Create a `template.FuncMap` with functions like `upper` (strings.ToUpper), `lower` (strings.ToLower), and `date` (time.Format). Register it with `template.New("funcs").Funcs(funcMap)`. Print results using `fmt.Printf("Upper: %s\n", ...)`.
hints: FuncMap is map[string]interface{} where values are functions
Functions must have 1-2 return values (second is error)

verification.failureMessage: Print results of upper, lower, and date functions.

steps.title: HTML escaping and safe content
steps.description: Demonstrate auto-escaping: render `"<script>alert('xss')</script>"` and show it's escaped. Use `template.HTML` type to render trusted HTML. Use `template.URL` for safe URLs. Print both escaped and raw output using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: template.HTML marks a string as safe HTML
template.URL marks a string as safe URL

verification.successMessage: HTML escaping and safe content work!
verification.failureMessage: Print both escaped and safe HTML content.
